automod.label: Auto-moderation
automod.description: Automatically filters spam, ads, abuse, and honeypot messages.

setupHoneypot.label: Create the trap channel
setupHoneypot.help: Creates a channel visible to everyone where writing triggers the configured sanction.
setupHoneypot.confirm: Create a new trap channel on this server?

msg.noPermission: Creation refused: the “Manage Channels” permission is missing.

honeypot.topic: Anti-compromised-account honeypot: do not send messages here.
honeypot.embedTitle: DO NOT SEND MESSAGES IN THIS CHANNEL
honeypot.embedDescription: This channel is used to catch compromised accounts. Any messages sent here will result in an immediate ban.

g0.label: ⚙️ General
g0.description: The trap channel is created with the “Create the trap channel” action below.

logChannelId.label: Automod log channel
logChannelId.help: The channel where every automod action is recorded: which rule fired, on whom, and the original message. Without it, sanctions land with nobody able to check they were deserved — this is the first channel to set up before enabling any rule.

ignoredChannelIds.label: Ignored channels
ignoredChannelIds.help: The automod looks at no message there. Keep it for channels where the rules make no sense: a meme channel full of capitals, a link-sharing channel, a test channel.

ignoredRoleIds.label: Ignored roles
ignoredRoleIds.help: Members holding any of these roles are out of reach of EVERY rule. Put the staff here: otherwise a moderator pasting three links in a row gets sanctioned by their own bot.

enabled.label: Enable
enabled.help: Sanctions a member sending too many messages in too little time. It is the rule that fires most often, and the only one that stops a raid in progress.

action.label: Sanction
action.help: What the bot does when the rule fires. Against spam, a temporary timeout is the only one that actually stops it: deleting messages lets the author carry on, and banning on a false positive costs you a member.

maxMessages.label: Max messages
maxMessages.help: The number of messages that trips the rule. Going below 4 also catches lively conversation: three people excited about a match easily write more than that.

windowSeconds.label: Window (s)
windowSeconds.help: The window those messages are counted in. What matters is the ratio: 5 messages in 10 seconds is spam; 5 in 60 is a conversation.

timeoutMinutes.label: Timeout (min)
timeoutMinutes.help: How long the timeout lasts, when that is the chosen action. Discord caps it at 28 days. A few minutes are enough to break up spam: it is an interruption, not a sentence.

enabled.label: Enable
enabled.help: Spots invites to OTHER Discord servers pasted in messages. Invites to this server are not affected.

action.label: Sanction
action.help: What the bot does on finding an invite. A warning is almost always enough: most invite links are pasted by well-meaning members sharing a friend's server.

enabled.label: Enable
enabled.help: Sanctions a message mentioning too many people at once. It is the rule against notification harassment, where someone pings fifteen people in a single message.

action.label: Sanction
action.help: What the bot does once the threshold is crossed. The mentions have already gone out by the time the bot reacts, so deleting the message does not undo the notifications: only a timeout stops it continuing.

maxMentions.label: Max mentions
maxMentions.help: How many mentions are tolerated in a single message. Note that @role counts as one mention, not as the number of members it reaches.

timeoutMinutes.label: Timeout (min)
timeoutMinutes.help: How long the timeout lasts, when that is the chosen action. Discord caps it at 28 days.

enabled.label: Enable
enabled.help: Sanctions messages written mostly in capitals. The rule most prone to false positives: acronyms, game titles, languages without lower case.

action.label: Sanction
action.help: What the bot does with an all-caps message. Deleting is enough: shouting is not an offence that warrants a timeout.

minLength.label: Minimum message length
minLength.help: Below this length a message is ignored however many capitals it has. This is what stops « OK », « LOL » or an acronym being sanctioned.

percent.label: % of capitals that triggers it
percent.help: The share of capitals above which a message counts as shouting. Below 70% it starts catching messages that merely contain an acronym.
